links.title: CatchBench: When Can an Agent Failure Be Caught?

evidence: Abstract: 'The release scores 72 entrants, from rule scanners and structural models to eleven LLM judges across nine model families (GPT, Claude, Gemini, Gemma, Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral, Nova), over 1187 declared configurations and 1162 recorded runs.'

Section 3.3: 'Sixteen comparison families are declared before scoring, and the contrasts inside each are adjusted by Holm's step-down procedure... all 118 reported contrasts are regenerated from the committed predictions.'
Section 5.4: 'The auditable lift over size (flat) is +0.141 on SWE-Gym (0.804 against 0.663). This is the paper's only effect that survives multiplicity correction.'

Section 4.3 Bar Verdicts: 'File-level Gold passes item 1... fails item 2... Named-value Gold v2 leaves items 1 to 3 undetermined... Thus both substrates remain mechanism diagnostics and carry no evidential weight.'

Appendix D.1: 'The injecagent harvester writes each roster as the user tool followed by the attacker tools... A rule that reads nothing but position... scores 1.000 F1 there' — a construction leak in the authors' own PRE corpus.
Reproducibility Statement: 'The scored board calls no model service: it reads committed prediction caches, so a third party reproduces every number in this paper without an API key.'
llm_evaluation.rationale: Highly on-topic: a benchmark for auditing LLM-agent failures scored across PRE/LIVE/POST information states, entrants include 11 LLM judges (GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, etc.), directly matching top-weight preferences for agents/tool use, LLMs, and LLM-as-judge evaluation. Novelty is solid rather than fundamental: the evidence-budget axis (three information states under one task-method interface) and a five-item admissibility bar for injected faults are new for agent auditing (Table 1 shows no prior benchmark covers all three states), but the fixed-data/many-method arena contract is inherited from ADBench/BOND. Rigor is exceptional: 16 pre-declared comparison families, 118 Holm-corrected paired contrasts, per-board floors, seed-stability analyses, and honest separation of 'separates' from 'unresolved' (47/118). The paper even documents and repairs its own harness defects (PyGOD batching bug, judge parser bug, injecagent declaration-order leak). Evidence is strong and internally consistent, with the headline SWE-Gym structural gain (+0.141 ROC-AUC, Section 5.4) the only effect surviving correction, and GPT-5.5's localization lead (0.452 vs 0.211) cleanly established; caveats include single-pass judge generations and small corpora that leave many contrasts unresolved. Generalizability is limited by domain split: structural signal holds on SWE-Gym but tau-bench remains an acknowledged open problem, and all three Gold-derived boards ship only as mechanism diagnostics after failing the authors' own admissibility bar. Reproducibility is outstanding: public repo, committed prediction caches allowing API-free rescoring, pinned corpus commits, CI checks, and documented PII redaction, though raw upstream traces must be fetched and judge regeneration needs credentials.

primary_link.title: CatchBench: When Can an Agent Failure Be Caught?

papers.summary: When can an agent failure be caught? An audit is usually limited by the record rather than by the method. CatchBench therefore puts one auditor's question to three information states: the declared configuration before a run (PRE), a growing prefix of its trace (LIVE), and the finished trace (POST). Prior benchmarks fix one of these states or vary the telemetry; to our knowledge none scores all three under one task-method interface. Each state admits different questions, so seven task contracts c
papers.summary_zh: 本論文提出 CatchBench，是首個在單一任務—方法介面下，跨三種資訊狀態評測 AI 代理稽核方法的基準：執行前的宣告設定（PRE）、執行中的軌跡前綴（LIVE）與執行後的完整軌跡（POST）。作者主張稽核成效受限於紀錄本身而非方法，故設計七項任務契約，涵蓋過度授權稽核、失敗早期預警、線上錯誤偵測、步驟定位、失敗偵測與原因歸因，形成九個計分板，收錄 1187 個宣告設定與 1162 筆執行紀錄，評測 72 個方法，包括規則掃描器、結構化偵測器與九個模型家族的十一個 LLM 評審。主要結果：118 個預先宣告的比較僅 47 個在 Holm 校正後可分離；GPT-5.5 在 Who&When 定位任務以 Top-1 0.452 領先所有非 LLM 方法；SWE-Gym 失敗偵測的結構特徵效應（0.804 對 0.663）是唯一通過校正者，而 tau-bench 的早期預警始終低於 0.70 警戒線。論文也揭露自身資料的缺陷：某語料來源保留宣告順位，一條只看位置的規則即達完美 F1，顯示分數反映語料建構方式而非推理能力；注入式 Gold 資料因留下可被偵測的建造痕跡，未通過五項可採納性檢驗，三個 Gold 計分板僅列為機制診斷。限制包括多數比較無法解析、標籤流程異質且部分仰賴 LLM 判讀、遺失接地與線上過期狀態偵測等問題仍未解。其價值在於證明基準分數須先公開標籤產生流程並檢驗捷徑才可解讀，並以預先宣告、無需模型呼叫即可重現的統計契約，取代單一排行榜式的結論。
papers.title: CatchBench: When Can an Agent Failure Be Caught?
papers.title_zh: CatchBench：代理失敗何時能被察覺？

links.title: From Inertia to Objectivity: Improving Deep Research Agents with Noise Isolation

evidence: Abstract: NIS-Agent achieves competitive performance while reducing token cost by 33% vs the smolagents DR baseline; code publicly available at github.com/PangSMPang/NIS-Agent
Section 3.2 / Appendix A.4: IBIS construction — 1,016 LLM-generated candidates filtered to 712, human annotation retains 245 Should Re-search + 209 Should Visit Page samples, Fleiss' kappa = 0.684
Section 6.2: switching Agentic to Observer Mode improves Should Re-search accuracy ~15–30% across models; GPT-4o collapses to 4.08% in Agentic Mode (Appendix B.1 Table 7)
Appendix A.5: paired flip analysis — 91.9% of flips point toward the inertia direction; 18 surface features fail to predict flips (AUC 0.498 direction, 0.492 occurrence)
Section 6.4 Table 4: GAIA/GPT-4o ablation — full NIS-Agent 61.82 vs w/o Filter 59.39 vs w/o Validation 56.96; Table 3: total tokens 219.8k → 147.3k (−33.0%)
Table 5: validation module transfers to math reasoning — AIME 2025 GPT-4.1 improves 35.3 → 68.7 vs CoT validation
Section 5 + Appendix D: NIS-8B trained on Qwen3-8B via SFT (4,293 examples) then GRPO (9,964 examples) with offline rubric generation (Claude Sonnet 4) and cheap online judge (qwen3-max)
Section 8 Limitations: no mechanistic investigation of the bias; generalization beyond information seeking and math is speculative; isolation filters can mistakenly discard relevant pages
Appendix C.4.2: full WebWalkerQA (680 queries) run with Claude-3.7-Sonnet yields 69.26% vs 68.50% on the 200-query subset, supporting subset reliability
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core LLM-agent research: diagnoses a newly named agentic failure mode ('inertia bias'), builds a controlled diagnostic benchmark (IBIS), proposes context-isolation interventions (NIS-Agent), and trains an 8B model via SFT+GRPO to internalize resistance. Hits high-weight preferences squarely (Agents & Tool Use, LLMs, Reasoning, RL/alignment, evaluation/benchmarks, RAG/grounding). Novelty is solid but context isolation/pruning is a known tool family; the contribution is the targeted debiasing framing plus controlled Agentic-vs-Observer measurement. Rigor is above average: paired conditions, Fleiss' kappa 0.684, ablations, token-cost analysis, AIME transfer, a subset-reliability check on full WebWalkerQA, and a paired flip analysis (AUC ~0.50 on surface features) that preempts the main confound. Evidence is strong across multiple benchmarks and backbones, though some baselines are self-reproduced, the noise analysis is manual and small-scale, and the 'inertia bias' construct is distinguished from confirmation bias mainly conceptually. Honest limitations (no mechanistic account, unverified generalization to other agent domains, isolation can discard relevant pages). Code release and detailed training/evaluation protocols support reproducibility, with some dependence on proprietary judges/teachers.

primary_link.title: From Inertia to Objectivity: Improving Deep Research Agents with Noise Isolation

papers.summary: Web search agents powered by Large Language Models (LLMs) show strong promise, but deep research tasks expose a recurring failure mode: once an agent has produced a query, plan, or intermediate conclusion, it becomes less objective when later judging the consequences of that same action. We term this phenomenon inertia bias. To make it measurable, we introduce the IBIS benchmark, which controls the search observations while varying whether the model is evaluating the outcome of its own prior act
papers.summary_zh: 本文探討 LLM 網路搜尋代理在深度研究任務中的系統性失敗機制:慣性偏誤(inertia bias)。一旦代理產生查詢、計畫或中間結論,之後評估該行動後果時便失去客觀性,傾向強化自己先前的選擇。作者建立 IBIS 基準,在相同搜尋結果下比較「自己發起行動」(Agentic Mode)與「外部資訊」(Observer Mode)兩種情境,發現模型普遍出現 15% 至 30% 的落差,證實此偏誤普遍存在。此偏誤會在兩個決策點放大雜訊:工作者層級的搜尋雜訊與管理者層級的脈絡雜訊。為此提出 NIS-Agent,於網頁篩選與答案驗證兩個脆弱環節導入情境隔離,使判斷脫離代理自身的行動歷史:過濾模組僅依任務狀態評估網頁並適時改寫查詢,驗證模組則重組推理鏈、逐項檢驗推論。在 GAIA、WebWalkerQA 等基準上,NIS-Agent 達到開源框架中的最佳表現,於 BrowseComp 亦具競爭力,並節省 33% token 成本;以 SFT 加 GRPO 訓練的 8B 開源模型 NIS-8B,在同框架下平均表現接近 GPT-4o。驗證模組附加於 ReAct 管線亦可大幅提升 AIME 數學推理成績,顯示方法可外推至深度研究之外。限制方面,作者僅將模型視為黑箱,未探究偏誤的機制根源;偏誤是否通用於程式碼或具身代理仍屬推測;隔離與驗證本身可能誤刪相關頁面或背書錯誤結論,高風險場景應保留人工把關。本文為代理系統的自我強化錯誤提供可量測的診斷基準與去偏介入方案,對建構更可靠的研究型代理極具參考價值。
papers.title: From Inertia to Objectivity: Improving Deep Research Agents with Noise Isolation
papers.title_zh: 從慣性到客觀:以雜訊隔離改進深度研究代理人

links.title: When "Do Not" Is Not Deny: Security Rules in CLAUDE.md vs Built-In Controls

evidence: Abstract & §I: 481 public CLAUDE.md files; only about 4–16% of retrieved security rules have a matching built-in control; strict adjudicated estimate 4.4% [2.6, 6.7]
§IV-B Table II: classifier precision 0.350, recall 1.000 on the matching-control judgment; annotator agreement 96.5% with Cohen's κ=0.89 (match) and 0.77 (security-relevant gate)
§III-E & §VI: blind 50-file audit puts rule-word extraction recall at 66.3% [48.8, 82.0], so rates apply only to retrieved rules
§IV-E Table VI: sampling-frame replication on Agent READMEs corpus gives 25.1% [20.8, 30.0], still a minority; same instrument, not independent confirmation

§III-D & Appendix A: post-hoc audit of frozen control reference found three documentation issues (additionalDirectories reversed, missing sandbox.credentials, imprecise network sandbox) with no label changes reported
Appendix D: releases frozen sampling frames, commit-pinned manifests, seed 20260813, frozen classifier prompt (Claude Sonnet 5), control-reference audit, and analysis scripts
llm_evaluation.rationale: Empirical usable-security measurement of LLM coding-agent instruction files: how often security rules written in CLAUDE.md have a matching built-in Claude Code control. Strongly aligned with Agents & Tool Use and AI Safety preferences (agent permission controls, tool-use enforcement, guardrails, agent misbehavior context), with secondary fit to Code & Programming and LLM topics; not a pure domain application. The research question (coverage of developer-written security rules by existing controls) is genuinely new relative to Agent READMEs, Cursorrules, ContextCov/Prose2Policy, and Michael & Roesner, though the method is standard corpus-mining plus LLM classification with human validation. Rigor is unusually high: stratified 180-item validation with inverse-probability weights, repository-clustered bootstrap CIs, two blind annotators (κ=0.89 match gate, 0.77 security gate) with adjudication, extraction-recall audit, duplication/concentration sensitivities, second-frame replication (25.1%), and a transparent post-hoc audit of the frozen control reference showing no label changes. Evidence is solid but the headline is a wide 4–16% range driven by the matching standard rather than sampling error, classifier precision for matches is low (0.350), and extraction recall (66.3% [48.8, 82.0]) restricts the denominator. Generalizability is honestly bounded to Claude Code at a freeze date and a capped, relevance-ranked GitHub frame; frame B reuses the same instrument. Reproducibility is excellent: frozen frames, commit-pinned manifests, seed, frozen prompt, control reference plus audit CSV, and analysis scripts released.

primary_link.title: When "Do Not" Is Not Deny: Security Rules in CLAUDE.md vs Built-In Controls

papers.summary: In CLAUDE.md, "do not" is a natural-language instruction that the model interprets. Claude Code's deny is a built-in control that blocks an action before the agent can take it. Both can express the same security goal, but they control the agent in different ways. We measure this gap in 481 public CLAUDE.md files. An LLM matched the extracted candidate rules against Claude Code's documented controls, and two security practitioners independently checked a sample without seeing the model's answers
papers.summary_zh: 論文量測一個可用性安全落差：開發者在 CLAUDE.md 以自然語言寫安全規則，但 Claude Code 只有 deny、ask 等 permission rule 與沙箱等內建控制能確定攔阻；兩者形式相同、強制力不同，檔案與工具都不標示何者真有控制支援。作者蒐集 481 個公開 CLAUDE.md，以規則詞抽出 4,661 個候選片段，用 LLM 分類器對照凍結的官方控制清單，判斷各片段是否為安全規則、有無免寫程式碼的內建控制；再由兩位安全實務者盲測 180 個分層樣本，以逆機率加權與儲存庫群集 bootstrap 校正。結果顯示，依配對標準寬嚴不同，僅約 4–16% 的已抽取安全規則有對應控制，最嚴格估計為 4.4%（95% CI：2.6–6.7%），其餘只能靠模型詮釋；破壞性命令與網路出口較常有控制，授權與個人資料最少（此排名屬探索性）。分類器 recall 高但 precision 僅 0.350，常把可比對的命令或路徑誤判為完整涵蓋；兩位標註者對配對判定高度一致（Cohen's κ=0.89）。抽取召回率為 66.3%，比率因此僅適用於被抽出的規則。限制：樣本取自 GitHub 程式碼搜尋、非隨機；研究僅測書面規則與文件記載的控制，未涵蓋團隊以 CI、hooks 等其他方式的防護或執行期可靠性。CLAUDE.md 因此是「只寫不回」的安全通道，對缺乏安全背景的新手風險最大，作者呼籲平台標示規則有無控制支援、把無法強制者列為建議，並使執行可被觀察。
papers.title: When "Do Not" Is Not Deny: Security Rules in CLAUDE.md vs Built-In Controls
papers.title_zh: 當「Do Not」不等於 deny：CLAUDE.md 安全規則與內建控制的落差

links.title: Feedback That Backfires: Why Small Language Model Agents Repeat the Call They Just Watched Fail

evidence: Section 6.1, Table 3: corrective gain negative for all 6 checkpoints with CIs excluding zero (e.g., SmolLM2-135M G=-23.92 [-25.86,-22.09]; Qwen3-0.6B G=-21.50 [-25.07,-18.18])
Section 6.2 and Table 5: decomposition attributes most of the effect to the surface-form term (copy 21.69 vs sem 2.23 for SmolLM2-135M), supporting the 'harness not model' claim
Section 6.5, Table 6: CodeRepair (MBPP with real interpreter output) shows the same per-token effect (~-1.09 to -1.23 nats/token across 3 models), guarding against ToolShed-specific artifacts
Section 7, Table 7: 'do not repeat' instruction moves repetition the wrong way (+0.16 [+0.06,+0.27] for SmolLM2-135M) while abstraction moves it by an order of magnitude (-21.68 [-23.20,-20.14])
Section 7.1: controls include a fail_other placebo (-13.71 [-15.33,-12.20], reported as a conservative lower bound), abstract_min variant, and length-matched neutral observation (copy 14.50 vs 16.64)
Section 8.3, Table 8: rollouts with Qwen2.5-0.5B on 24 tasks; drop harness raises exact repeat rate 0.31 to 0.80, ban reduces it to 0.08, but task success does not improve (+0 [+0,+0])
Section 10/11: limitations stated plainly - ladder stops at 1.7B (hardware-bound), 18% of actions are prose-not-call at this scale, greedy-only rollouts, ToolShed is author-built

Section 9 and Appendix A: CPU-only reproduction (i7-6820HQ, PyTorch 2.4.0+cpu), base seed 20260808 with named sub-streams, measured Transformers version drift of 4.9e-5 nats, NaN-guard after a lost run
Abstract and Section 6.1: aggregate claims (0.06 to 0.54 repeat probability; 19% greedy exact repeats) arithmetically consistent with Table 4 per-model values
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core in-scope LLM-agent methodology: a controlled token-level measurement of whether appending failed tool calls/error messages to ReAct-style transcripts helps small LLMs (Agents & Tool Use and LLM preferences, high weight), plus MBPP program repair (Code & Programming). Novelty is solid but not maximal: repetition self-reinforcement, negative-instruction weakness, and context contamination are known (the paper's Table 1 positions itself honestly); the new contributions are the corrective-gain metric, the counterfactual copy/sem decomposition, and decomposition-derived interventions including the counterintuitive finding that clean restart is the worst harness. Rigor is strong for the study's scale: teacher-forced deterministic scoring, task-clustered bootstrap with Holm correction, fixed perturbation operators for byte-identical items across models, placebo and length-matched controls, cache-free re-scoring verification, and an explicit failure analysis (Sections 7.1, 10). Evidence is internally consistent across two environments (~-1.03 nats/token in both) with CIs excluding zero on 90-100% of items, but rollout confirmation is limited to one model on 24 tasks, and the interventions reduce repetition without improving task success (honestly reported in Section 8.3). Generalizability is the main limit: ladder stops at 1.7B, ToolShed is self-built, rollouts are greedy-only; the authors explicitly decline to extrapolate (Section 11). Reproducibility is exemplary: full code/data release, CPU-only pipeline, base seed with named sub-streams, pinned environments with measured version drift, and verbatim prompts (Appendices A, F).
topics: small language models (SmolLM2, Qwen2.5, Qwen3, Llama-3.2)

primary_link.title: Feedback That Backfires: Why Small Language Model Agents Repeat the Call They Just Watched Fail

papers.summary: Agent harnesses record a failed tool call and its error message in the transcript and ask the model to continue, on the assumption that the error is corrective information. We measure whether it is. Defining the corrective gain of a failure record as the change in log-probability of re-emitting the action that just failed, we find the gain is negative for every instruction-tuned model we tested (6 checkpoints, 135M-1.7B, 4 families) in two environments: simulated tool calling and MBPP program re
papers.summary_zh: 代理框架慣於把失敗的工具呼叫與錯誤訊息附加到對話紀錄，假設錯誤回饋具有矯正性。本文實測得到相反結論：作者定義「矯正增益」，即紀錄失敗前後重新產出該失敗動作之對數機率的變化，在六個指令微調模型（135M–1.7B、四個家族）與兩種環境（模擬工具呼叫 ToolShed，及含真實 Python 直譯器輸出的 MBPP 程式修復）中一律為負，約每動作 token −1.03 nats，且在九成以上個別項目成立；固定候選集合上，重複失敗呼叫的機率由 0.06 升至 0.54，貪婪解碼在失敗後有 19% 項目逐 token 重現失敗呼叫。透過反事實觀察（分別回報失敗、成功或僅中性確認）分解，83% 的損害來自失敗呼叫表面字串誘發的複製效應，而非模型讀不懂錯誤；語義項既小且在不同環境下正負號不一致，故問題出在框架而非模型。據此，以執行時期產生的失敗描述取代逐字呼叫可消除 76% 的反轉，於解碼器封鎖已失敗字串亦有效且近乎零成本；加註「不要重複」指令無效；而依先前文獻建議清空上下文重試，反而使逐字重複率自 31% 暴增至 80%，是所有框架中最差者。核心原則：失敗後的上下文必須異於失敗前，且差異不得正是失敗動作本身。限制包括僅測至 1.7B 模型、於 CPU 以 float32 執行、失敗動作由固定擾動算子合成，且兩項介入雖降低重複卻未提升任務成功率（主要失敗來源是模型能力上限）。此結果對以小型模型建構代理極具實務價值：廉價的框架層級修改即可避免卡死迴圈。
papers.title: Feedback That Backfires: Why Small Language Model Agents Repeat the Call They Just Watched Fail
papers.title_zh: 適得其反的回饋：小型語言模型代理為何重複才剛目睹失敗的呼叫

links.title: MobilePA-Bench: Benchmarking Mobile Planner Agents on Complex Real-World Tasks

evidence: Abstract: benchmark spans 13 functional domains and 212 realistic mobile tools; best model reaches 75.52% overall
Section 4.1: 1,705 tasks split as 1,040 Basic Tool Use, 89 Sub-agent, 376 Memory, 200 Skill; recall N=15, max step budget T_max=15
Section 3.3.1: three evidence-aligned Query Buckets (Tool Call, State Change, Agent Behavior) each paired with a dedicated checker
Section 3.5 / Eq. 12: fixed overall score weighting 0.50 Basic, 0.10 SubAgent, 0.20 Memory, 0.20 Skill, without external justification
Section 4.3 / Table 4: three-run stability of Qwen3.6-27B with Overall std 0.22 and range 0.41 points
Section 4.4-4.6: per-dimension results with counts, e.g., Claude-Opus-5 at 872/1,040 Basic, Qwen-3.8-Max 243/376 Memory, 312/400 Skill trajectories
Section 4.7: claims that models issue 'premature, hallucinated tool calls' are qualitative, without quantitative error-type breakdown
Contributions (Section 1): 'We fully open-source our complete infrastructure—including all 1,705 benchmark tasks' with GitHub URL https://github.com/Tongyi-MAI/MobilePA-Bench
Section 3.4: clarifies the 1,530-query scenario snapshot is descriptive and separate from the 1,705-task evaluation denominator
llm_evaluation.rationale: In-scope LLM-agent benchmark paper squarely aligned with top-weighted preferences (agents & tool use, LLMs, multi-step planning, memory, RL-readiness). It contributes a stateful mobile OS sandbox with 1,705 tasks, 212 tools, and a four-dimension evaluation (basic tool use, sub-agent collaboration, memory, skill usage), showing the best of 13 frontier LLMs at only 75.52% overall. Novelty is moderate: the unification of sub-agent/memory/skill evaluation inside an interactive sandbox is new relative to GUI-centric (AndroidWorld, MobiBench) and static function-calling (BFCL, DroidCall) benchmarks, but each component is established (TAU-bench-style statefulness, MemGPT-style memory, VOYAGER-style skills). Rigor is solid with formal verification buckets, fixed 50/10/20/20 aggregation, and a three-run stability analysis (Overall std 0.22), but Bucket 3 rubric-based behavior checking, the unexplained weighting scheme, and absence of ablations (e.g., tool recall N=15) or inter-annotator agreement weaken it. Quantitative evidence is clearly reported with task counts (e.g., 872/1,040; 312/400), though headline failure-mode claims in Section 4.7 are qualitative without error-type quantification. Findings are somewhat mobile-specific, but the capability dimensions and open infrastructure generalize. Full open-source claim with a GitHub repository and standardized settings support good reproducibility, tempered by reliance on proprietary frontier models.

primary_link.title: MobilePA-Bench: Benchmarking Mobile Planner Agents on Complex Real-World Tasks

papers.summary: As on-device LLM agents evolve into personal copilots, the mobile operating system has become a key testbed for this paradigm, making rigorous capability evaluation essential. Yet existing benchmarks fall into two camps, each with a critical blind spot: GUI-centric benchmarks test surface-level screen manipulation while overlooking background tool use and long-horizon planning, whereas static function-calling benchmarks rely on offline API matching that is detached from real runtime constraints.
papers.summary_zh: 行動裝置上的 LLM 代理正演變為個人副駕，但現有評測各有盲點：以 GUI 為中心的基準（如 AndroidWorld、OSWorld）僅測螢幕操作，忽略背景工具呼叫與長程規劃；靜態函式呼叫基準（如 BFCL、DroidCall）則仰賴離線比對，脫離真實執行時的系統限制。作者提出 MobilePA-Bench，一個互動式、有狀態、以工具為中心的評測基準：在可執行沙盒中維護即時應用程式資料庫並回傳結構化回饋，涵蓋 13 個功能領域、212 個擬真工具與 1,705 個真實任務，系統性評測四個維度——基本工具使用、子代理協作、記憶使用與技能使用；驗證依完成證據分為工具呼叫、狀態改變與代理行為三類查詢桶，再以 50/10/20/20 固定權重彙總總分。實驗涵蓋 13 個前沿模型，最佳者 Claude-Opus-5 整體僅 75.52%，且 13 個模型中有 7 個低於 70%；基本工具使用最佳達 83.85%，記憶使用（33.78%–64.63%）與子代理協作明顯偏弱，無單一模型於所有維度稱霸；在嚴格呼叫順序、權限阻擋與執行期錯誤下，表現更大幅下滑，顯示複合可靠度不足。限制方面：沙盒為模擬環境，未涵蓋真機像素級視覺操作；記憶與技能以人工標註的 gold ID 作為額外閘門，可能偏嚴；子代理僅評測路由與交接品質而非下游執行。總體而言，此基準兼具診斷價值與適合強化學習的高吞吐量互動環境，並完整開源，有助於打造可信賴的行動代理。
papers.title: MobilePA-Bench: Benchmarking Mobile Planner Agents on Complex Real-World Tasks
papers.title_zh: MobilePA-Bench：在複雜真實世界任務上評測行動規劃代理的基準

links.title: PROOF-Gen: From Optimized Data to Better Distillation

evidence: Abstract: per-scenario optimization recovers 93% of failed scenarios; Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 improves Pass^1 0.132→0.529; Gemma 4 E4B-it +7.2pp on BFCL v4 multi-turn
Section 2: cheatsheet appended to teacher system prompt, stripped before training ('scaffold removal'), K=10 iterations using GEPA optimizer
Table 2/Section 3: recovery rate 93.0% telecom (279/300 sampled of 2,013 failures) vs 33.7% BFCL (89/264); teacher pass rates 7.3% vs 52.9%

Section 4 RQ2/Figure 4: filtered-only training improves partial rewards (action accuracy +25pp) but not end-to-end task completion in any of four model–benchmark pairs; combined training is the only condition with consistent gains

Figure 3/Table 8 (Appendix A.2, F): reflector ablation on 82 cross-domain failures, recovery 24.4% (GPT-4o self-reflection) to 97.6% (GPT-5.1); 264/279 telecom recoveries cheatsheet-driven, 15 stochastic replay
Table 3 (Appendix A.3): GPT-5.1 high-reasoning direct generation 83.3% vs GPT-4o+GPT-5.1 reflector 93.0% vs GPT-5.1+1 reflection step 98.3%; reflector averages 2.2 calls per scenario
Table 14 (Appendix N): retrain/re-eval stability, Pass^1 0.518–0.538 across independent runs, spread 0.020
Table 4/Appendix B.1, C: integrity audit of 90 trajectories by Claude Opus 4.6 (90/90) and Sonnet 4.6 (88/90, both flags false positives on manual inspection); exact judge prompt in Figure 9

Section 4 RQ3: production deployment +6.3pp trajectory goal completion, +1.5pp on-device model goal completion, positive transfer in every locale (non-English avg +1.48pp); absolute values withheld per deployment policy, single large-scale run

Limitations/Appendix J: template-level disjointness not enforced on τ²-bench splits; sole teacher GPT-4o; cheatsheets reach 7–9K chars so executor instruction-following assumption is binding and unmeasured; BFCL per-category n=60 results exploratory
Table 12/Appendix M: BFCL gains concentrate in miss_func (Gemma 0.0→15.6, Qwen 11.7→31.7), other categories mixed; overall accuracy stable across 3 runs (spread ≤1.6pp)
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core LLM/agent distillation methodology paper squarely matching top-weighted preferences (LLMs 2.5, Agents & Tool Use 2.5, Training/Optimization, Prompting). The contribution—inverting per-scenario prompt optimization into a disposable data-generation instrument that recovers teacher-failed trajectories, then stripping the scaffold before SFT—is a genuinely new twist relative to STaR/ReST/Agent-R (which assume a passing trajectory exists) and ACE (which deploys playbooks at inference); the capability–voice decoupling analysis is a nice secondary insight. Rigor is above average: reflector-capability ablation across four models (24.4%–97.6%), frontier direct-generation comparison (Table 3), partial-credit baseline showing filtered-only improves action accuracy +25pp but end-to-end completion in none of four model–benchmark pairs, retraining/re-evaluation stability checks (Pass^1 0.518–0.538), a 90-trajectory integrity audit with reproduced judge prompts, and a candid Limitations section (template-level split leakage, single teacher, unmeasured instruction-following bound, n=60 category noise up to 3.3pp). Evidence is strong on public benchmarks but weaker for the production study (pp-only deltas, single run, absolutes withheld) and flip-task robustness uses post-hoc selected small subsets (n=46/21). Generalizability is decent—two benchmarks, two student families, multi-locale deployment—but bounded by one teacher, one reflector provider, and the requirement of an execution-based verifier. Reproducibility is moderate: hyperparameters, judge rubrics, and cheatsheet examples are released in appendices and models/benchmarks are public, but no code/data release is claimed and part of the evaluation is internal.

papers.summary: Supervised fine-tuning on teacher-generated trajectories is the standard first stage for distilling tool-calling capabilities into deployable models. Post-training pipelines that drive shipped tool-calling agents re-run this stage on a daily or weekly cadence, paying the frontier-teacher cost each cycle, yet the mechanism is generate-and-filter (keep the teacher's passing trajectories, discard the rest) and each cycle leaves behind the same hard scenarios because failures supply no signal. papers.summary_zh: 標準的教師—學生蒸餾流程是「產生後過濾」：保留教師通過的工具呼叫軌跡、丟棄失敗者，最難的情境因此永遠缺席於訓練資料。τ²-bench 上 GPT-4o 有 57% 試驗失敗，其中三分之二是「差一步」的近似成功——多數工具呼叫正確，卻因單一關鍵錯誤全盤皆輸；而部分得分訊號不足以補救。PROOF-Gen 對每個失敗任務進行逐情境提示詞最佳化：反思器（GPT-5.1）以 GEPA 分析失敗軌跡與驗證器回饋，撰寫糾正用「小抄」附加於教師系統提示，令教師從頭重跑直到通過；訓練前移除小抄，學生只從乾淨示範學習。此設計將解題能力（反思器）與互動風格（執行者）解耦，實現保留產品語氣的蒸餾。結果：telecom 領域救回 93% 的抽樣失敗情境，反思器能力主導——GPT-5.1 達 97.6%，GPT-4o 自我反思僅 24.4%。以合併資料微調後，Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 在 τ²-bench 的 Pass^1 由 0.132 升至 0.529，Gemma 4 E4B-it 在 BFCL v4 多輪提升 7.2 個百分點；僅用過濾資料無法提升端對端完成率。生產部署中軌跡品質提升 6.3 個百分點，裝置端模型跨語言環境皆正向轉移。限制：僅驗證單一教師與同供應商反思器；方法假設執行者能遵循長達 7–9K 字元的結構化小抄；公開基準任務量有限，部分類別結果僅屬方向性。本研究首度以自動提示詞最佳化作為資料產生引擎，補上重訓流程對困難情境的覆蓋缺口。

links.title: What Process Evaluation of Coding Agents Actually Measures: Action, Task, and Step Are Three Different Levels

evidence: Abstract/§1: introduces SCAE, a replay-based estimator from a structural causal model, and experiments on 499 file-localization episodes from 12 repositories; claims next actions driven by execution provenance, uncertainty at task level, and collider bias in full-trace judges.

§4.2/Figure 3(a): on the 67.0% first-visit steps, a provenance-only predictor reaches top-3 = 0.326 [0.276, 0.375] vs 0.058 for a deliberately strengthened code-graph predictor and 0.072 for repository frequency.

§4.5/Figure 5: instance identity explains residual replay variance with ICC = 0.640 vs permutation null 0.196 (p=5e-4); 0 of 190 intervention-estimated step effects survive BH-FDR at q=0.10 despite 1901 replays over 12.7 hours.

§4.6/Figure 6 and Table 5: full-trace judge verdict moves +0.537 later in normalized position (59/70 episodes, sign test p=1.1e-16), replicated across 3 judges (displacement p=0.181 for heterogeneity) while enrichment is model-dependent (heterogeneity p=0.044).

Appendix D.2 (Table 12): pre-registration record including entries that failed (entropy-vs-position monotonicity, v0 LORO AUROC 0.481 vs >=0.60 threshold) and retirement of the D1 disagreement criterion at observed 97.1%.
§5 Limitations: scope confined to file localization; corpus 46% django; only 46.2% of agent objects resolve to graph nodes; intervention reference formally identified but empirically weak.
Appendix D.1: all numbers regenerated by seed-fixed CPU-only scripts with macro verification; §4.1 reports replayability 1.00 over 100 actions and 0 compaction events.

Appendix B.4: positivity probe based on only 10 probed decision points across 3 episodes; Appendix C.6: three-way uncertainty decomposition validated only on a synthetic generating process (recovery correlation 0.994), not real traces.
llm_evaluation.rationale: A methodological paper on process evaluation of LLM coding agents that cleanly aligns with high-weight preferences (Agents & Tool Use, LLMs, Code & Programming, Evaluation/LLM-as-judge, interpretability of attribution). Novelty is solid: a three-level decomposition (action/task/step), SCAE as a structural-causal-model-based replay estimator, and a controlled judge-information manipulation isolating collider bias are fresh contributions, though they build on known Gumbel-max counterfactual machinery and prior agent-evaluation work. Rigor is unusually high: formal identification results with proofs, pre-registration record (including four failed predictions and one retired criterion), BH-FDR control, permutation/closed-form nulls, and honestly reported negative results (0/190 step effects survive FDR; v0 AUROC 0.481 at chance). Evidence is strong for the headline claims (provenance vs. code graph with CIs; ICC 0.640 vs 0.196 null; collider displacement +0.537, sign test p=1.1e-16, replicated across 3 judges), but weakened by small samples in places (10-point positivity probe across 3 episodes, 23-episode cross-judge subset) and an uncertainty decomposition validated only synthetically. Generalizability is limited by the paper's own scoping: file-localization only, django-dominated corpus, and 46.2% graph-node coverage. Reproducibility is strong internally (seed-fixed scripts, environment pinning verified at 1.00, macro verification), though no explicit public code/data release is stated.

primary_link.title: What Process Evaluation of Coding Agents Actually Measures: Action, Task, and Step Are Three Different Levels

papers.summary: Coding agents are increasingly evaluated not only by whether they solve a task, but also by how they execute it. However, existing process-level evaluations often treat action prediction, task uncertainty, and step attribution as if they were the same problem, which makes it unclear what such evaluations actually measure. In this paper, we introduce a measurement framework for process evaluation in coding agents and instantiate step-level causal attribution with SCAE, a replay-based estimator de
papers.summary_zh: 本文主張，程式代理的過程評估長期混淆三個不同的分析層級：動作層（代理下一步會做什麼）、任務層（整體執行的不確定性）與步驟層（某一步是否因果地改變最終結果）。作者提出測量框架，並以 SCAE——一個源自結構因果模型、透過回放估計步驟局部因果效應的工具——加以實作，在 499 個檔案定位片段上驗證。主要證據：下一步動作主要由執行足跡（代理剛在工具輸出中看到的路徑）驅動，而非程式碼依賴圖的結構轉移；執行不確定性主要結構化於任務層級而非步驟層級；全軌跡 LLM 評判者在下游步驟可見與否之間呈現系統性對撞偏差位移，顯示其測量的多半是語義相關性而非經認證的因果貢獻。限制包括：僅限可回放的檔案定位情境、介入式步驟參考未通過 FDR 校正、回放預算使步驟級歸因在可行成本下統計力量不足。此研究的價值在於提醒：過程獎勵模型、全軌跡評判與重啟消融各測不同量，其輸出應依實際測量的層級詮釋，而非自動視為步驟級因果歸因。
papers.title: What Process Evaluation of Coding Agents Actually Measures: Action, Task, and Step Are Three Different Levels

links.title: The Compaction Cliff in Long-Running AI Agent Memory

evidence: Abstract/§4.3 Figure 3: Claude Code /compact on Sonnet 4.6 preserves 53% of safety rules after one compaction round and 10% after five on 20 production agent configurations.
§4.3 Table 6: TypeCompact reaches 1.00/0.95/0.80 constraint recall at 50/25/10% compression vs 0.53/0.39/0.24 for the best type-blind compactors across 20 AAC configurations.
§4.3 Table 7: TypeDecompose 0% mean locality violations vs 93% for chunk_by_tokens on 200 AAC configurations, at +14.5% mean token overhead.
§4.3 Table 8: TypeRetrieve reaches 100% recall@50 vs 73% for the best single-shot LLM retriever, using zero LLM tokens per query.
§4.4 Table 9 and Setup: reference labels come from gpt-5.4-mini, so recall for gpt-5.4-mini-based variants measure self-consistency; human agreement κ=0.45 five-class, 0.79 constraint-vs-other.
§4.5: SafetyMed (N=200) preservation 95.5% vs 81.0% for Sonnet single-shot (McNemar p=3.7e-9); τ-bench retail 37.7% vs 28.6% full and 29.2% hierarchical (p=0.003/0.005, N=329 pairs).

§4.5 Discussion: retail comparison is equal-policy but not equal-tokens (TypeCompact 1,136 vs hierarchical 669 tokens); airline footprint reverses (647 vs 718) while TypeCompact still leads (p=0.024).

§5 Limitations: MaRS-FL is the authors' reimplementation (no public implementation); multi-round rollout run on two of four LLM families; public-GitHub sourcing may not transfer to enterprise corpora.
Reproducibility footnotes 1–2: AgentArtifactCorpus released on HuggingFace and classifier/reference code on GitHub.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Highly on-preference work on LLM agent memory/context management with a safety framing: type-blind compaction silently drops agent safety rules ('Compaction Cliff'), addressed by Knowledge Triage, which routes typed items through per-type retention policies across compaction, decomposition, and retrieval. Novelty is moderate-to-good: pinning safety-critical items verbatim is a simple core mechanism, but the typed rate-distortion framing, per-operator guarantees, and multi-round production-prompt quantification are a genuine contribution beyond prior typed-memory systems (MaRS, MemGPT) which lack per-type guarantees. Rigor is strong: 10 compaction baselines across 4 LLM families plus structural baselines (§4.3, Table 6), component-removal ablations, McNemar tests on three behavioral benchmarks (§4.5), inter-annotator agreement (κ=0.92 preserved/lost, §4.5), and a candid limitations section (self-referential classifier labels, κ=0.45 five-class, MaRS-FL reimplementation, non-token-matched retail comparison). Evidence is solid but not airtight: classifier evaluation uses gpt-5.4-mini labels as reference (§4.4), behavioral gains partly confounded by larger retained footprint (1,136 vs 669 tokens, §4.5), five-round decay tested on only two of four LLM families (§5), and the claimed formal proofs of §3.3 are only sketched in the visible text. Generalizability is supported by five public corpora, cross-domain benchmarks (retail/airline/medical), and a 396,934-item corpus, though public-GitHub sourcing and small behavioral sets (N=115/50/200) limit scope. Reproducibility is good: released HuggingFace dataset, classifier, and reference code (footnotes 1–2), though dependence on proprietary models (Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4.7, gpt-5.4 family) limits full replication.

When the budget overflows, both are summarized at the same rate; only the rule needs exact wording to remain enforceable. On 20 production agent configurations, Claude Code's /compact prompt on Sonnet 4.6 preserves 53\% of safety rules after one compaction round and 10\% after five. We name this the Compaction Cliff. We address it with Knowledge Triage, a framework that classifies each line of an agent's know
papers.summary_zh: 長期運作的 AI 代理中，安全規則與情節日誌爭奪相同的上下文 token 預算。本文發現所謂「壓縮斷崖」：Claude Code 的 /compact 在 Sonnet 4.6 上經一輪壓縮僅保留 53% 的安全規則，五輪後降至 10%。為此作者提出知識分診框架，將代理知識庫中的每一項分類為五種型別（約束、程序、信念、偏好、情節），並以三個確定性運算子分流：TypeCompact 依型別設定保真度就地壓縮、TypeDecompose 將過大主題分割並複製範圍內的安全規則、TypeRetrieve 在檢索時優先釘住適用規則。在五個公開語料上，TypeCompact 於每個壓縮比保留的安全規則是最強單次 LLM 壓縮器的 2–4 倍，五輪後仍有 96% 召回率；TypeDecompose 達到 0% 局部性違規；TypeRetrieve 達到 100% recall@50。下游行為基準（醫療合規、零售任務通過率、航空領域）證實工件層級的保留可轉化為更安全的代理行為。限制：語料取自公開 GitHub、安全保證完全依賴分類器召回率、分區複製開銷波動大。作者同時釋出包含 396,934 個代理知識工件的 AgentArtifactCorpus，對部署中的代理安全深具意義。

links.title: InjecMEM: Memory Injection Attack on LLM Agent Memory Systems

evidence: Abstract: 'achieving up to 35.4% retrieval success rate (RSR) and 76.6% attack success rate (ASR)' on MemoryOS, with code at https://github.com/BlueBlood6/InjecMEM
Sec. 3.2 (Threat Model): attacker has black-box memory subsystem, single interaction, no read/edit access to store, but white-box access to backbone LLM is assumed
Table 2: Multi-GCG reaches 76.6% ASR-c and 35.6% ASR-j while DPI, BadChain, and GCG all score 0.0 on both metrics
Table 3: MemGPT evaluation gives RSR 37.2, ASR-c 48.6, ASR-j 18.1 using a command optimized on MemoryOS
Table 5: CF-Multi-GCG optimized on Qwen+Mistral transfers to both (70.5/43.2 ASR-c) but scores 0.0 on Llama-3.1-8B; Concat-3 achieves 78.2/66.3/75.4 across all three backbones
Table 4: 7B-optimized command transfers to fine-tuned 7B (75.6) but fails on 3B/14B (0.0) until Family-Joint optimization (36.8/64.2)

Appendix A, Table 6: LLM-as-a-Judge/ProtectAI/PromptGuard defenses only reduce ASR-j to 26.7-29.8 with ~0 benign blocking; perplexity at tau=40 fully suppresses attack but blocks 71.8% of benign pages

Appendix B (Limitations): admits strongest attacks require backbone white-box access and the attack targets memory systems that store original interaction text, leaving rewrite-heavy pipelines to future work
Appendix C.2, Table 8: WildChat real-user evaluation reports Health RSR@1 64.7±7.02, ASR-j 46.0±5.29 over three seeds
Appendix C.1: released corpus of 944 conversations / 3096 pages across 19 domains plus ~1900 evaluation queries 'available in the project repository'; experiments use 10 random seeds (Sec. 4.1)
App. E (Generation Setup): target output is a fixed insult string with neutral marker matching by normalized string match, a relatively weak success criterion
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core LLM-agent security paper squarely matching top preferences (agents, AI safety, red teaming, memory/RAG): it formalizes a single-shot memory injection attack on LLM agent memory systems with no store access, a clear threat model, and formal RSR/ASR metrics. Novelty is moderate rather than high: it builds on established GCG-style optimization and is differentiated from AgentPoison (direct store edit) and MINJA (multi-turn, trigger-keyed) mainly by single-shot budget, topic-conditioned anchor design, and Multi-GCG robustness to variable placement/context drift; Appendix D itself maps these deltas. Rigor is solid: 19 domains, 10 seeds, ~50 queries/domain (Sec. 4.1), ablations over anchor types and joint optimization (Tabs. 1,5), defense evaluation (App. A, Tab. 6), and a WildChat real-user check (App. C.2, Tab. 8). Evidence is generally supported by tables, though all-zero ASR baselines (Tab. 2), a crude fixed-string success criterion (App. E), a white-box backbone assumption (Sec. 3.2), and a small RSR aggregation inconsistency between Tab. 1 averages and Tab. 3 temper confidence. Limitations are candidly stated (App. B): reliance on white-box optimization and systems storing raw interaction text; cross-family transfer fails without concatenation (Tab. 5). Reproducibility is good: public code link, released corpora (944 conversations, 3096 pages, ~1900 queries), surrogate prompts, pseudocode (Algs. 1-4), and optimized commands (App. F), though some hyperparameters (T, W, K, m values) are not fully enumerated.

primary_link.title: InjecMEM: Memory Injection Attack on LLM Agent Memory Systems

papers.summary: Memory is becoming a default subsystem in deployed LLM agents to provide persistent personalization and continuity. This naturally prompts a question: will memory system introduce new vulnerabilities into agents? Thus we propose InjecMEM, a novel memory injection attack paradigm that requires only a single interaction (no read/edit access to memory store) to steer later responses of related queries toward a pre-specified output. Guided by the retrieval-then-generate mechanism of memory systems,
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出 InjecMEM，一種針對 LLM 代理記憶體系統的注入攻擊：攻擊者僅需一次互動、無需讀取或編輯記憶體儲存，即可使後續相關查詢的回應被導向預定輸出。攻擊由兩部分組成：一是與檢索器無關的錨點，含高召回的主題線索，使受污染紀錄持續被檢索；二是透過 Multi-GCG 梯度座標搜尋、在多個合成上下文與插入位置上平均最佳化的對抗指令，以對抗上下文漂移、位置變動與長提示稀釋。在 MemoryOS 與 MemGPT 上，攻擊達到最高 35.4% 的檢索成功率與 76.6% 的條件攻擊成功率，且在良性記憶漂移下持續有效，非目標查詢大致不受影響。轉移實驗顯示：家族內聯合最佳化可提升對未見變體（含微調版本）的轉移；跨家族則可靠簡單串接多條指令同時覆蓋。防禦評估顯示常見檢索期過濾器（LLM 評判、ProtectAI、PromptGuard）防護有限，困惑度過濾雖可完全阻擋攻擊但會誤擋 71.8% 良性頁面。限制：主要適用於儲存原始互動文字的系統，且指令最佳化仰賴對骨幹模型的白盒存取。此研究將記憶體系統確立為一個安全邊界。

links.title: Safety Hacking in Constrained Best-of-$N$ Inference-time Scaling

evidence: Abstract: defines safety hacking as selecting an output that passes the learned constraint but violates the true safety criterion; finite-N bounds governed by joint upper reward tails.
Theorem 4.1: finite-N bounds for CBoN hacking probability in terms of joint tails Ψ_A, Ψ_B; Theorem 4.2 gives asymptotic certainty under tail separation (Section 4).

Section 6.2: 714 test prompts from JailbreakBench/HarmBench/AdvBench; 256 samples per prompt from Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (228,608 candidates), Llama-Guard-3-8B filter, beaver-7b-v1.0-reward ranking, HarmBench classifier as operational safety criterion, gpt-5-mini safety-aware reward.

Section 6.2 Reward-proxy ablation: Beaver CBoN hacking 9.1% (N=1) to 13.4% (N=256); Skywork decreases to 6.8%; unsafe-only term 1.6% under both, competitive term 11.7% -> 5.3%, attributing trend to reward ranking.
Appendix A.15: equal-tail control (σ_B=σ_A=0.2) drives hacking to zero by N=32 and no-false-positive control gives zero hacking, supporting the tail-amplification mechanism.
Section 7 Limitations: analysis restricted to fixed, non-adaptive i.i.d. candidate pipeline; explicitly excludes adaptive search, self-refinement, tree search, and agentic planning.
Appendix A: full proofs for Theorems 4.1/4.2/5.1, Corollary 4.3, Propositions 5.2/A.6/A.8-A.10, plus cPes pseudocode (Algorithm 1) and consistency result A.8.
Appendix B.2: ShieldGemma-2B alternative-filter sensitivity (12.1% -> 14.8% hacking, competitive term 0 -> 13.8%) reported as qualitative consistency rather than primary evidence.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Directly on LLM inference-time scaling safety: formalizes 'safety hacking' where reward maximization amplifies false acceptances of a learned safety filter in constrained Best-of-N. Strong match to LLM (Qwen2.5-7B experiments), AI Safety, Alignment (reward models, SafeRLHF lineage), and Red Teaming/Evaluation (JailbreakBench, HarmBench, Llama Guard, ShieldGemma) preferences. Theoretically substantive: finite-N tail bounds, asymptotic inevitability result, chi-square coverage-control theorem with proofs, plus a pessimistic sampling algorithm. Evidence is unusually careful: 228,608-candidate pool, permutation-averaged estimates with cross-prompt standard errors, a two-term finite-N decomposition, reward-proxy ablation (Beaver vs Skywork reversing the trend), and alternative-filter sensitivity. Deductions: formalization builds closely on existing reward-overoptimization and pessimistic BoN work; LLM evidence is limited to one generator model on adversarial prompts with modest effect sizes (9.1%->13.4%) and non-ground-truth operational criteria (HarmBench classifier, gpt-5-mini rubric); theory explicitly excludes adaptive/tree/agentic search, limiting scope; no explicit code release despite detailed model/checkpoint/rubric specifications.

papers.summary: Inference-time pipelines often sample multiple outputs, filter them with a learned safety model, and return the proxy-feasible output with the highest learned reward. We show that this composition creates a two-stage failure: an imperfect safety proxy first contaminates the feasible set with unsafe outputs, and reward maximization can then amplify this residual contamination. We define \emph{safety hacking} as selecting an output that passes the learned constraint but violates the true safety cr
papers.summary_zh: 受限 Best-of-N（CBoN）推論時運算先以習得的安全模型過濾取樣，再以獎勵模型挑選最高分輸出。本文定義「安全駭取」為選中通過習得安全約束但違反真實安全準則的輸出，並指出兩階段失效：不完美的安全代理先污染可行集，獎勵最大化再放大殘留污染。理論上，有限 N 界由代理可行集中安全與不安全輸出的聯合獎勵上尾主導：若不安全但可行者具有較重上尾，隨 N 增大安全駭取漸近趨於必然，即使誤接受質量與平均代理誤差皆趨於零。與代理可行參考分佈保持有界 χ² 散度的策略（如受限悲觀取樣 cPes）可獲得與 N 無關的駭取上界，但只能限制放大、無法修復污染。玩具與 LLM 實驗（Qwen2.5-7B、Llama Guard 過濾器、Beaver 獎勵代理）以有限 N 分解證實：競爭性不安全勝出項隨 N 上升，是駭取率成長的主因；改用 Skywork 獎勵代理可反轉此趨勢，凸顯獎勵尾行為的關鍵角色。限制：僅分析固定非自適應管線，未涵蓋自我精煉或樹搜尋等回饋式程序。結論指出安全的推論時縮放需同時控制進入可行集的污染與下游集中。

links.title: Beyond Factual Knowledge: Benchmarking and Learning Step-Level Procedural Rule Reasoning in Large Language Models

evidence: Abstract: claims DynaRule improves average QA accuracy by up to 19 points and achieves over 85% Recall@1 at 10K rules
Table 2 (Rule Num = 10000): DynaRule avg 0.5700 vs SR-KI 0.3712, consistent with the claimed ~19.9-point gap
Table 4 / Table 10 (Rule Num = 10000, FOL): DynaRule Recall@1 0.8613 vs SR-KI 0.2415, matching the claimed 61.98-point retrieval gain
Section 5.1: confidence layer identified as argmin of layer-wise attention entropy; Stacked Step-Level Attention Loss with <search> token and gold-rule hard negatives (Eq. 3-5)
Appendix B (Evaluation Settings): 10 samples per task type per seed, 110 per seed, 550 questions total; exact match on comma-separated boxed answers
Appendix C.4: five seed-level scores with standard deviation and t-based 95% CI half-widths reported per method and rule scale
Section 6.4 (Generalization to Unseen Rules): 50.20% overall exact match at 10K rules on a rule repository disjoint from training, 6.80 points below the original split
Section 6.4 (Efficiency Analysis): KV injection scales as O((M+N)N) with TTFT/memory/throughput measured on one A800 for Qwen2.5-7B
Limitations: rules limited to FOL and NL forms; evaluation capped at 10,000 injected rules versus millions; embedding-only representations may lose information
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core LLM-methodology work squarely on high-weight preferences (LLMs, reasoning/CoT, RAG & knowledge, KV-cache memory). Contributions: RuleWorld, a 4.94M-rule / 3.37M-QA synthetic benchmark for reusable procedural rules with single-rule, parallel multi-rule, and multi-hop QA, and DynaRule, a KV-cache injection method adding confidence-layer identification (lowest attention entropy, layer 23 for Qwen2.5-7B) and Stacked Step-Level Attention Training with a learned <search> token. Novelty is solid but incremental: the injection mechanism builds directly on KBLaM and SR-KI, and the advance is step-wise retrieval supervision rather than a new architecture. Rigor is good overall — prompting, dense/BM25/hybrid RAG, IRCoT, ReAct, KBLaM and SR-KI baselines across 100–10K rules in FOL and NL, ablations (rule-removal collapse, gold-rule-only, held-out rules, iterative RAG, efficiency), and seed-level std/95% CIs (Appendix C.4). Weaknesses: evaluation uses only 10 samples per task type per seed (550 questions per setting, Appendix B), the benchmark is fully synthetic with LLM-merged questions, DynaRule is trained/evaluated end-to-end on a single base model (Qwen2.5-7B) on the authors' own benchmark, and cross-model work covers only confidence-layer identification. Quantitative claims are internally consistent (e.g., 19.88-point avg gain and 61.98-point Recall@1 gap at 10K rules match Tables 2 and 10), supporting above-average evidence strength. Code/dataset release plus detailed hyperparameters and prompts aid reproducibility.

primary_link.title: Beyond Factual Knowledge: Benchmarking and Learning Step-Level Procedural Rule Reasoning in Large Language Models

papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) excel at text understanding and generation, yet still struggle to reliably understand and apply externally provided procedural rules at scale. To evaluate this capability, we introduce RuleWorld, a large-scale benchmark that reformulates rules as globally reusable abstract units rather than instance-specific facts. In RuleWorld, several scenarios, including single-rule, parallel multi-rule, and multi-hop reasoning, are settled for comprehensive evaluation. We further
papers.summary_zh: 現有基準多將程序性規則當成逐題提示，忽略規則作為可重複使用的共享知識本質。本文建立 RuleWorld：包含 494 萬條抽象、無常識依賴的程序性規則（一階邏輯與自然語言雙形式），衍生 337 萬個 QA 實例，涵蓋單規則、平行多規則與多跳推理共 11 個子任務。方法上提出 DynaRule：以預訓練句編碼器將規則對齊後注入 KV cache，先透過注意力熵辨識「信心層」，再以疊接步驟級注意力訓練，於推理步驟前插入特殊 <search> token 觸發規則重新注意與 KV cache 更新，使檢索成為內部可學習的逐步過程。實驗顯示現有 LLM（含 GPT-5.5、DeepSeek V3.2、Claude）在大量規則注入下劇烈退化，而 DynaRule 平均 QA 準確率提升最多 19 點，10K 規模下 Recall@1 超過 85%，領先最強基準逾 60 點。限制：僅以嵌入表示規則可能損失資訊、評估上限為 10K 規則、多跳仍受早期檢索錯誤傳播影響。此工作凸顯參數知識與顯式規則落地之間的落差，對政策遵循等程序性推理應用具有直接意義。

links.title: The Dialect Tax: Dialectal Biases Persist throughout the Language Modeling Pipeline

evidence: Abstract: character-level counterfactual tokenizer 'removes neither input and output asymmetries nor dialectal accuracy gaps', establishing the bias is model-induced, not tokenizer-induced alone
Section 3.1/Figure 2: AAVE mean fertility gap of +0.07 tokens/word across all seven tokenizers, with Kendall's W=0.89 (p<0.001) confirming ranking stability across tokenizer families (Appendix D.1)
Section 3.2/Table 12: SAE-AAVE reasoning gap for all model families and sizes (delta -1.49 to -5.73 pp) with McNemar's test and Holm-Bonferroni correction on ~300 samples per condition

Section 4/Figure 3: accuracy gap does not systematically change under character tokenization (five models widen, four narrow, insignificant sign and paired t-test); Table 1 shows dialect still decodable from hidden states above 86% under character tokenization

Section 5.1/Figure 5: all nine base models assign significantly higher cross-entropy to AAVE (mean gap ~0.56 nats, one-sided paired Wilcoxon Bonferroni-corrected p<0.001, dz in [2.12,2.55]); gradient divergence z=-2.64 vs unrelated-SAE baseline using CountSketch with d=8,192 buckets

Section 5.2/Tables 14-17: eight of ten RMs reject E[Delta r]=0 at p<0.05 with task-dependent sign flips (Algorithm +0.43, Planning -0.14, |d|<=0.25), while dialect-exclusive tokens receive higher isolated rewards than SAE-exclusive ones (pooled gap -0.55, p<0.001), showing contextual vs lexical decoupling

Limitations: authors state experiments are observational, involve 'no model training', cannot repeat across random seeds, cover only English dialects, and datasets differ in construction (human rewrites vs rule-based translation)
Appendix A/B: code open-sourced on GitHub; Tables 5-7 enumerate exact Hugging Face tokenizer, LM, and RM model IDs; compute described as 8x NVIDIA L4 and 8x A5000 servers
llm_evaluation.rationale: A core LLM fairness/bias paper tracing dialectal disparities across tokenization, pre-training gradients, post-training reward models, and inference-time representations of modern open LMs (Llama-3, Gemma-3, Qwen-3, plus GPT for reasoning). Strongly aligned with LLM (w2.5), AI Safety (w2.0), Alignment/RM analysis (w2.0), Interpretability probing (w1.8), and NLP/tokenization (w1.5); no Japanese-LLM content. Novelty is solid rather than exceptional: it synthesizes existing corpora (ReDial, ParallelAAVE, MultiVALUE) and prior component-level findings, but the pipeline-wide trace, the character-tokenization counterfactual, CountSketch gradient-geometry analysis (z=-2.64, dialect pairs less aligned than unrelated SAE documents), and the decoupling of isolated-token vs in-context RM preferences are genuinely new contributions. Rigor is high: Holm/Bonferroni-corrected Wilcoxon, McNemar, Friedman and Kendall's W tests, null baselines (character perturbations, translations, unrelated documents), correctness-confound checks (pooled r=-0.013), and honest reporting that AAVE gradient divergence sits within the character-noise range (Table 2) and that RM effect sizes are small (|d|<=0.25) and sign-flip by task. Evidence is quantitative and multi-modal but partly observational: authors admit no training ablations, no multi-seed runs, and English-only scope; the income correlation (Fig. 11) is speculative. Generalizability is limited to English dialects and mid-size open models, though methodology transfers. Reproducibility is good: GitHub code link (Appendix A), full Hugging Face model IDs (Tables 5-7), dataset reconstruction details (A.1), and perturbation probabilities, though manual GPT-5 Mini data fixes and unspecified seeds slightly reduce it.

primary_link.title: The Dialect Tax: Dialectal Biases Persist throughout the Language Modeling Pipeline

papers.summary: Systematic dialectal performance gaps in language models (LMs) are well documented, but the source of these disparities within the modern language modeling pipeline remains unclear. Our study traces this "dialect tax" across the natural language processing pipeline. Using parallel English dialect corpora that hold meaning fixed while varying surface form, we first confirm that LMs recognize matched Standard American English (SAE) and dialectal texts as semantically equivalent. However, we discov
papers.summary_zh: 本文以英語平行方言語料（SAE 與 AAVE 等，語義固定而表面形式不同）系統性追蹤「方言稅」在語言建模管線各環節的分布。研究首先驗證模型確實將對應方言對視為語義等價，接著揭露：現代分詞器仍對方言文本產生更高的 fertility 與 token 長度；以字元級反事實分詞器繞過子詞切分，既無法消除輸入與輸出熵的不對稱，也無法縮小準確率落差，且方言身分仍可從隱藏狀態以高準確率線性解碼。預訓練階段：方言配對產生的梯度更新比兩份完全無關的 SAE 文件更為分歧，且 AAVE 輸入的交叉熵損失持續偏高，此損失落差與答對與否無關。後訓練階段：獎勵模型呈現情境相關的不穩定偏好——孤立方言專屬 token 反而得分更高，完整推理上下文中卻受到任務與模型相依的方言懲罰。限制：語料多為規則生成或社群文本、僅限開源模型、缺乏受控訓練消融。整體結論是方言偏見並非源自單一環節，而是在分詞、預訓練、後訓練與推論各步驟中累積，改善需要管線層級的整體介入。

links.title: What Proves You Wrong: Benchmarking Language Models on Falsifiable Research Ideation

evidence: §4.1/Table 1: strict ordering GPT-5.2 > Claude Sonnet 4.6 > GLM-5 > DeepSeek-V3.2 recovered in all 10,000 bootstrap replicates from 950 order-stable of 1,200 folded cases; second judge (Doubao Seed 2.0 Pro) reproduces the identical ordering with 86.1% stable-comparison agreement (§4.1, Appendix E.5).

§4.2: single-field manipulation check—clean proposals win 40/40 ordered comparisons per corrupted dimension (grounding/metric/falsifiability) with target-score drops 1.73/2.00/1.95; subtle-corruption audit shows sham-equivalence gate passing (0 clean wins vs sham) with adjusted preferences 0.550/0.775/0.537 and CIs excluding zero.

§4.3: human calibration covers 20/200 neighborhoods, 90 real pairs, 3 annotators; 87.2% agreement (34/39) with judge on decisive stable cases and 11/12 naive-control detection, but Krippendorff's α=0.238 (winner selection) bounds validation strength.
§6 Limitations: single canonical judge per version, no execution of proposed tests, domain restricted to ML-adjacent literature, and benchmark-wide human validation explicitly not established.

Appendix B.3 and G.2: orientation defect in 65 reverse tasks disclosed and corrected; construction seed 20260620, bootstrap seeds documented, raw API responses archived, benchmark and audit artifacts released on GitHub.
llm_evaluation.rationale: An LLM evaluation-benchmark paper squarely within the curator's LLM/evaluation preferences: it measures whether frontier LLMs can produce falsifiable research proposals judged via LLM-as-judge with order-bias auditing. Novelty is real but compositional: the six-field falsifiable-test contract as the judged unit is new per their own survey (Table 2, Appendix F.2), while pairwise judging, position-bias folding, and human calibration are acknowledged established primitives. Rigor is unusually strong: 2,400 ordered judgments with order folding, Bradley-Terry plus Condorcet, pair-level and context-cluster bootstraps (Appendix C.3), a disjoint second judge replication (86.1% stable-case agreement, Appendix E.5), manipulation checks with sham contrast (40/40 clean wins; adjusted preferences with CIs excluding zero, §4.2), and candid disclosure of weaknesses (Krippendorff's α=0.238, 65.6% validator agreement, 3.9% naturalness leakage, orientation defect in 65 batch-1 tasks, Appendix B.3/D.3). Evidence is internally consistent (Table 3 head-to-head sums check out) and claims are appropriately bounded, but the headline ordering rests on a single closed-source LLM judge per version, human corroboration covers only 20/200 neighborhoods with 3 undergrad annotators, and modest inter-annotator agreement limits validation strength. Generalizability is constrained to ML-adjacent OpenReview literature with no cross-domain evidence. Reproducibility is good (frozen outputs, documented seeds, verbatim prompts, released repo) but dependent on closed preview APIs.

primary_link.title: What Proves You Wrong: Benchmarking Language Models on Falsifiable Research Ideation

papers.summary: Large language models are increasingly used to propose research ideas, yet the prevailing ways of judging such ideas supply no shared decision rule: free-form judging sways with style and position, and scoring against a later paper rewards recovery of one realized trajectory. We introduce a benchmark that carries a proposal from Literature to Test: the Lit2Test benchmark centers on a six-field contract organized around a falsifying outcome, so that every proposal precommits the observation that
papers.summary_zh: 自由格式評審易受風格與位置影響，以未來論文當答案鍵則只獎勵單一已實現路徑。本文提出 Lit2Test 基準，以六欄位契約（文獻缺口、假說、最小實驗、決定性指標、支持結果、否證結果）為評測單元，要求每個構想預先承諾何種觀察會證明自己錯誤。基準由 200 個真實論文鄰域（800 篇論文）前瞻性構建、無答案鍵；四個前沿模型各產生一份提案，形成 1,200 個配對與 2,400 次雙向盲評。結果在所有 10,000 次 bootstrap 複製中皆恢復嚴格排序：GPT-5.2 > Claude Sonnet 4.6 > GLM-5 > DeepSeek-V3.2，250 個順序敏感案例被明確分離而非隱藏。診斷控制（渲染對照、單欄位操縱檢查、細微污染審計）顯示評審回應的是實質而非風格，分離主要來自測試與指標設計，否證性則如同准入門檻。三名標註者的分層人類校準以 87.2% 一致率佐證結論，但適度的標註者間一致度界定了宣稱範圍。此基準讓構想品質成為可由實驗判定的屬性，對可否證研究構想的評測深具意義。

links.title: STONIC: A Layered Measurement Contract for LLM Value Profiling

evidence: Abstract: 10 of 17 configurations preserve the endorsement-choice relation; all 17 eligible configurations prefer their own earlier answer (median effect 0.790); option position changes choice rate in every eligible configuration.

Section 3 (Measurement Contract): 35 configurations receive 5,144 situations from four banks across L1/L2/L3/L2* interfaces; 978,040 total requests; prespecified coverage (80% valid, 80 clusters), Holm-corrected aggregate, 3/4-bank direction, and leave-one-bank-out sign requirements.

Section 4 (Inference): 20,000 within-bank permutations for semantic nulls, 10,000 item-cluster bootstrap draws, Holm FWER .05 for predefined families, BH q=.05 exploratory; seeds 13/2026/20260817 yield identical corrected decisions.

Section 5 / Table 1: rating-predicts-choice supported for 10/17 estimable configurations (median +.228, all instruction-tuned); own-answer preference supported for 17 (range .508-.932); position sensitivity significant in 18/18 (median signed effect .0218); no configuration supports same-profile semantic transfer (median rho .73/.43/.50 diagnostic only).

Appendix K (Task-Local Human Validation): 200 L3 responses, three annotators per response, Fleiss kappa .415 presence / .403 four-state; FULCRA AUROC .893 on 91 matched rows, GPV->DeBERTa19 AUROC .784 with leave-one-bank-out F1 .629.

Section 7 (Limitations): banks do not represent all cultures/languages/deployment settings; strict parsing creates missing-not-at-random coverage especially for base models; hidden probes establish predictive information, not causality.

Appendix B/M (Reproducibility): byte-identical rebuild of request artifacts with SHA-256 digests; pinned vLLM 0.19.1 image, temperature 0, seed 13; model weights, raw generations, and hidden tensors are outside the arXiv source bundle.
llm_evaluation.rationale: A measurement-methodology paper squarely within LLM evaluation/alignment scope: it tests whether value profiles from ratings, counterbalanced choices, free text, and hidden states support a single claim across 35 LLM configurations and 5,144 situations. Preference relevance is high (LLM evaluation, alignment/safety measurement, probing, prompt/order sensitivity), not a pure domain application. Novelty is solid rather than groundbreaking: it builds on existing value benchmarks (ValuePortrait, FULCRA, Generative Psychometrics) but the layered measurement contract with prespecified eligibility gates and the L2* own-answer-preference test (median +0.790) are fresh contributions. Rigor is a standout: conjunctive cross-bank reporting criteria, A/B counterbalancing, Holm/BH correction, equal-bank weighting, leave-one-bank-out checks, seed sensitivity, and a 200-response three-annotator human audit (Fleiss kappa .415). Evidence strength is strong with complete per-configuration tables, CIs, and appropriately hedged claims (semantic transfer estimable but 0/35 meet all-bank coverage; hidden-state results framed as decodability, not causality). Generalizability is deliberately bounded by the authors (four non-representative banks, missing-not-at-random parse coverage, Schwartz-10 limits). Reproducibility is partially supported (fixed seeds, pinned vLLM runtime, SHA-256 request digests, prompt contracts) but raw generations/hidden tensors are excluded from the bundle, the code/data package availability is asserted rather than verifiable from the text, and several listed checkpoints (e.g., Qwen3.6, Gemma 4, GLM-4.7) cannot be independently confirmed, warranting modest deductions.

primary_link.title: STONIC: A Layered Measurement Contract for LLM Value Profiling

papers.summary: LLM value studies often merge questionnaire ratings, pairwise choices, and values inferred from generated text into one profile. That merge assumes that the three observations describe the same stable preference. STONIC tests this assumption on 5,144 situations from four banks and 35 fixed model configurations. It compares responses rated in isolation, choices made under counterbalanced conflict, spontaneous answers, and later choices between a model's own answer and authored alternatives. 10 of
papers.summary_zh: LLM 價值研究常將問卷評分、成對選擇與從生成文字推斷的價值合併為單一輪廓，STONIC 檢驗此假設。在四個情境庫的 5,144 個情境上，以 35 個固定模型組態比較孤立評分（L1）、雙向平衡的衝突選擇（L2）、自發回答（L3），以及模型自身答案與人工撰寫替代選項的對比（L2*）。結果顯示：10/17 個可用組態跨庫維持評分—選擇關係；全部 17 個合格組態都偏好自己稍早的答案（中位數 0.790），且選項位置在每個合格組態都顯著改變選擇率。輪廓傳遞由評分到衝突選擇最強、對自發文字最弱，且無一組態通過全庫語義覆蓋門檻，故證據不支援跨介面的單一價值身分。對 200 則 L3 回應的三方標註顯示 FULCRA 最接近人類多數，DeBERTa 校準後仍保留排序資訊；隱藏狀態對已完成的決策比僅提示更易解碼。限制包括覆蓋率不足、分數器相依，以及僅屬預測性（非因果）的探針證據。此測量契約的價值在於：每個觀察只能支持其介面特定的主張，遺漏應保持遺漏，而非補成中性值。

links.title: When Can Agents Safely Checkpoint, Fork, Restore, and Merge? Exact Checking for Execution Edits

evidence: Section I 'Contributions' (p.2): 'Lean mechanizes the finite checker and runtime invariant, and tests validate all six edit forms. The source code, Lean proofs, and executable tests are available in the public GitHub repository at https://github.com/eunomia-bpf/agent-check-restore-safety.'

Section VIII (p.13): 'Six Lean modules pass --trust=0'; 'All 19 paper-specific tests pass, together with 62 authorization and checker regression tests'; accepted instances with 2-128 results take '0.11 - 53.47 ms'.

Theorem 4, Necessary Record Information (p.12): 'If any one of the four parts is omitted wholesale while the others are retained, two records become indistinguishable even though the correct answer differs.'

Proposition 2 (p.11): output-sensitive bound O(D+nLambda+|Gcov|+VB log(2+VB)) and the caveat 'Exponential growth occurs only in explicitly emitted linearizations and pairs linking partial executions to required results.'
Section A-M (p.23): measurement protocol 'fresh CPython 3.12 process... median of five repetitions on a 16-vCPU AMD EPYC 7R12.'

AI Use Acknowledgment (p.24): OpenAI Codex 'used throughout the manuscript for initial prose drafting and revision, and in the executable artifact for code scaffolding and test generation... including definitions, assumptions, theorem statements, and proof structure.'
llm_evaluation.rationale: Strong on-topic match for Agents & Tool Use and AI Safety: the paper formalizes safe Checkpoint/Fork/Restore/Merge ('execution edits') in tool-using agent runtimes, deriving from a trusted execution record which edits are safe, with rejection proofs and an atomic rule update. It is not an LLM-methodology paper (the agent is an abstract untrusted principal; LLM agents appear only as motivating context and citations), so LLM/Japanese-LLM/reasoning preferences are not engaged. Novelty is substantial: prior recovery/synthesis work takes requirements as input, whereas this derives the complete safety condition, proves a largest safe execution set (Lemma 4), an information lower bound over four record parts (Theorem 4, Table II), and ideal-runtime weak bisimulation (Theorems 6-7). Rigor is high: full formal model, 17 lemmas and 7 theorems, Lean mechanization with --trust=0, and an output-sensitive complexity bound. Evidence is solid for the formal claims but the evaluation is synthetic (2-128 results, 19 paper tests + 62 regressions, millisecond timings) with no deployment on a real agent runtime, and worst-case behavior grows exponentially in emitted linearizations. Generalizability is tempered by strong assumptions: registered workflows, typed edit rules, signed policy authorities, finite registered call models. Reproducibility is good (public GitHub with Lean proofs and executable tests, described measurement protocol), though the disclosed use of Codex for refining definitions, theorem statements, and proof structure warrants some caution despite stated author verification.

primary_link.title: When Can Agents Safely Checkpoint, Fork, Restore, and Merge? Exact Checking for Execution Edits

papers.summary: Agent runtimes can Checkpoint an execution, Fork it, Restore a checkpoint, or Merge branches without restarting a task. We call these operations execution edits, with Checkpoint recording the current execution for later use and Fork, Restore, and Merge changing what the Agent will do next. An execution edit cannot undo an earlier authorization or a tool request already sent. An unsafe edit can therefore authorize the same tool action twice, discard a result the task still requires, or conflict w
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究代理執行期環境中的「執行編輯」操作：檢查點、分支、還原與合併。此類操作雖可支援探索與復原，卻可能重複授權同一工具動作、遺失任務仍需的結果，或與編輯前已發出的呼叫衝突。由於代理本身不可信任，執行期必須依賴執行紀錄判斷每次編輯必須保留的歷史授權與必要結果。作者提出精確檢查演算法：從執行紀錄列舉所有可行的完整執行方式，逐步剔除會使仍需結果無法完成的執行；若全數被剔除，則回傳可獨立驗證的拒絕證明，否則回傳最大的安全執行集合。論文涵蓋檢查點與六種分支、還原、合併形式，證明原子規則更新在多次編輯與重新啟動下仍維持安全，並以弱雙模擬證明執行期與理想原子機器的代理可見行為等價。資訊結果顯示工作流程結構、動作對應、授權進度與規則版本四個紀錄部分缺一不可。六個 Lean 模組完成形式化驗證，19 項論文特定測試與 2–128 結果規模的量測（接受案例 0.11–53.47 毫秒）支持可執行性。此工作為代理系統的分支與復原機制提供精確的安全條件與資訊下界，是代理執行期安全設計的重要基礎。

links.title: FormuEvo: LLM-Guided Evolution for Discovering Solver-Efficient Mixed-Integer Programming Formulations

evidence: Section 3.2-3.4: five specialized LLM modules; diagnostic LLM converts fine-grained solver statistics (root gap, node count, presolve) into 'verbal gradients' guiding crossover/mutation.
Section 4.2, Table 1: TSP FormuEvo 0.1410 SGM vs best baseline SCF 0.3079 (Easy); abstract claims up to 5.5x solver speedup.
Section 4.4, Table 3: removing Diagnosis or Memory degrades performance (e.g., TSP Hard 3.9469 -> 6.5207 without Diagnosis).
Appendix C.1, Table 6: paired Wilcoxon tests; BPP Easy p=2.82E-01 and QAP Easy p=4.44E-01 not significant, attributed to floor effect - honest negative reporting.
Appendix C.2, Tables 7-8: framework re-validated on COPT and SCIP, including FormuEvo-G transfer across solvers.
Section 4.5, Table 4: three backbone LLMs (GPT-5.4-mini, Claude-Sonnet-4.6, DeepSeek-V4-Flash) all beat best baselines, no single backbone dominates.
Section 4.3 / Fig. 4: distilled knowledge base transfers zero-shot to unseen problems and bootstraps smaller LLM (GPT-5.4-nano).
Appendix B: Algorithm 1 pseudocode and full operator prompts; code claimed at github.com/Xyz-yuanhf/formuevo.
Limitations section: framework restricted to static formulations; dynamic relaxation/decomposition methods (column generation, Benders) explicitly out of scope.
Section 3.2 Evaluation: correctness enforced by checking solved objective values against ground truth; failed candidates get one repair attempt, preserving membership in the valid formulation space.
llm_evaluation.rationale: A methodologically LLM-centric paper (not a pure domain application): FormuEvo uses five specialized LLM modules (generator, diagnostic, repair, reflector, distiller) as evolutionary operators over executable Gurobi modeling programs, squarely matching high-weight preferences for LLMs, code/program synthesis, and agentic tool orchestration. Novelty is moderate-to-good: LLM-guided evolutionary search is established (FunSearch, ReEvo, AlphaEvolve, EvoCut), but adapting it to holistic MIP formulation design, plus solver-statistics-as-verbal-gradients diagnosis and distillable structured memory, is a genuine contribution. Rigor is strong: five classical problems plus two novel tasks, expert and LLM baselines (ORLM, StepORLM, EvoCut), component ablations (Table 3), backbone ablations with API costs (Table 4), cross-solver transfer (Tables 7-8), public-benchmark generalization (Fig. 5), hyperparameter sensitivity (Table 9), and Wilcoxon significance tests with honestly reported non-significant Easy-level results (BPP 2.82E-01, QAP 4.44E-01, Appendix C.1). Evidence is quantitative and multi-axis, though evaluated largely on self-generated instance splits and correctness verified only by objective-value match (Section 3.2). Generalizability is well supported within optimization (multiple solvers, backbones, unseen problems, smaller models), but untested outside MIP. Reproducibility is aided by a public code link, full prompts (Appendix B), and detailed hyperparameters, but depends on proprietary LLM APIs and stochastic search. Limitations section honestly excludes decomposition-based methods.

primary_link.title: FormuEvo: LLM-Guided Evolution for Discovering Solver-Efficient Mixed-Integer Programming Formulations

papers.summary: Mixed-integer programming (MIP) lies at the core of operations research and industrial optimization. While large language models (LLMs) have recently shown promise in automated MIP modeling from natural language, they prioritize semantic correctness but overlook formulation strength, severely bottlenecking the efficiency of downstream solvers. We propose FormuEvo, an LLM-guided evolutionary framework for automated discovery of solver-efficient MIP formulations. FormuEvo frames MIP formulation de
papers.summary_zh: 混合整數規劃（MIP）的多種數學等價表述，其求解效率可能相差數個數量級。現有以 LLM 自動建模的方法著重語意正確性而忽略表述強度，使下游求解器效率受限。FormuEvo 將 MIP 表述設計視為在可執行程式構成的符號空間上的演化最佳化：以 LLM 驅動的交配、突變與修復操作，迭代生成、評估並挑選更強的候選表述。為避免盲目探索，本文導入求解器資訊診斷機制，將預解結果、鬆弛品質、分支規模等細粒度統計轉為可解讀的「口語梯度」，引導針對性改良；並以結構化記憶庫將經驗抽象為可重複使用的建模策略，支援零樣本遷移與小型模型增強。在 TSP、JSSP、BPP、CFLP、QAP 等線性與非線性基準及 NNV、IMO 等新穎任務上，FormuEvo 發現的表述大幅超越專家設計與現有 LLM 方法，加速求解器最高達 5.5 倍，蒸餾知識亦能有效跨問題與模型規模遷移；消融證實診斷與記憶皆為關鍵元件。限制在於僅針對靜態表述，尚未涵蓋欄位生成或 Benders 分解等動態方法，與分解式演算法的共同演化為未來方向。

papers.title_zh: FormuEvo：以 LLM 引導演化，發現求解器高效的混合整數規劃表述

links.title: Is Next-Chunk Reasoning RL Really Better than SFT? Revisiting Training Strategies under no-CoT Data

evidence: Abstract: Mixed SFT 'achieves a clearly higher post-RLVR performance ceiling than next-chunk reasoning RL while requiring over 60× less training compute', consistent across in-domain math and out-of-domain reasoning.
Table 1: survey of RPT, RLP, RMT, RLPT, PretrainZero showing all mark 'Mixed SFT' as ✗, supporting the claimed baseline gap.
Table 2: post-RLVR Mixed SFT reaches 87.50/85.73/70.42 on AIME24/25/26 and 9.24/60.98/75.84 on HLE/GPQA-Dia./MMLU-Pro, exceeding NTR (87.50/84.38/69.38) and NSR (85.52/80.92/72.19) averages.
Sec 3.3 / Fig 3: Mixed SFT has lowest pre-RLVR average (27.5) yet highest post-RLVR average (61.1), a 33.7-point gain vs 3.3–10.3 for other methods.
Sec 4 Observation 1 / Fig 5: high-entropy token pool shows no-reasoning accuracy ~0.48 throughout, implying the entropy filter admits locally predictable targets.
Table 3 and Appendix Table 8: inserting NTR or NSR between Mixed SFT and RLVR yields slightly lower post-RLVR scores (e.g., HMMT26 50.50/49.52 vs 51.52), ruling out a token-coverage confound.
Appendix G Table 9: entropy-controlled NTR scores lower than vanilla NTR on all nine benchmarks, supporting that collapse is not the cause of NTR's ceiling.
Appendix A Limitations: single fixed mixing ratio and math-only corpus/benchmarks; transfer to code, multilingual, or other domains untested.

Appendix B: full training details (Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base on H200s, lr 1e-6, GRPO, deduplication against eval benchmarks) and Table 5/6 hyperparameters and decoding configs; prompts in Appendix I; no code/data release statement found.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core LLM post-training study on reasoning (CoT, RLVR/GRPO, SFT vs RL on no-CoT data), strongly matching LLM, reasoning/CoT, RL, and training preferences. The contribution is a corrective, well-controlled comparison rather than a new method: Mixed SFT is a simple but genuinely overlooked baseline (Table 1 confirms prior NCR works never compared against it). Rigor is solid: five strategies from one base model, shared RLVR stage, six in-domain plus three OOD benchmarks, ablations inserting NTR/NSR after Mixed SFT (Table 3/8), an entropy-controlled NTR variant (Appendix G), and a retention probe (Table 4). Evidence is extensive and internally consistent, though single-model, single-mixing-ratio, math-only, and without variance estimates. The mechanistic analysis (entropy filter admitting locally predictable tokens, template collapse) is plausible but interpretive. Reproducibility is aided by detailed hyperparameters, decoding configs, and prompts, but no code or data release is stated. Limitations (fixed ratio, math domain) are candidly acknowledged.

primary_link.title: Is Next-Chunk Reasoning RL Really Better than SFT? Revisiting Training Strategies under no-CoT Data

papers.summary: Recent work proposes next-chunk reasoning RL for leveraging no-CoT data---corpora such as worked solutions and textbook derivations that contain reasoning-rich content but lack explicit chain-of-thought annotations. The method trains a model to generate implicit reasoning traces and rewards them by their ability to predict the next chunk of text. While promising, existing evaluations primarily compare against conventional SFT baselines, leaving open whether the gains come from the RL formulation itself or from more effectively exposing the model to no-CoT data. We address this question with a controlled study of next-chunk reasoning RL and a simple but previously overlooked alternative: Mixed SFT, a single supervised fine-tuning stage that jointly trains on no-CoT and long-CoT data. Despite its simplicity, Mixed SFT achieves a clearly higher post-RLVR performance ceiling than next-chunk reasoning RL while requiring over 60 times less training compute. The advantage is consistent across in-domain mathematical reasoning and out-of-domain reasoning tasks. Moreover, we show that higher pre-RLVR accuracy does not necessarily translate into higher post-RLVR accuracy, highlighting the need to evaluate no-CoT training strategies in the context of the full post-training pipeline.
papers.summary_zh: 近期提出的「下一區塊推理 RL」利用無 CoT 資料（如解答範例、課本推導）訓練模型生成隱式推理，並以能否預測下一段文字作為獎勵。然而既有評估僅對照在無 CoT 資料上的單純 SFT，無法釐清成效來自 RL 形式本身，或僅是更有效地暴露於此類資料。本文從同一基礎模型出發，在相同 RLVR 預算下比較 NTR、NSR、序貫式 SFT、混合式 SFT 與純推理 SFT。結果顯示混合式 SFT——在單一階段同時訓練無 CoT 與長 CoT 資料——在領域內數學與領域外推理上達到最高的 RLVR 後天花板，運算量少逾 60 倍。分析指出 NTR 的熵過濾並未選出真正需要推理的 token，生成軌跡退化為局部補全，抑制熵崩潰亦無助提升；混合式 SFT 的前段低分僅為暫時的格式錯位，可由 RLVR 修復，而序貫式 SFT 的第二階段會覆寫先前吸收的無 CoT 知識，RLVR 無法復原。本文提醒：應以完整後訓練管線評估無 CoT 策略，前置準確率無法預測最終表現，對受運算限制的實務者而言，SFT 階段的資料組成比額外 RL 階段更重要。
papers.title: Is Next-Chunk Reasoning RL Really Better than SFT? Revisiting Training Strategies under no-CoT Data
papers.title_zh: 下一區塊推理 RL 真的比 SFT 更好嗎？在無 CoT 資料下重新檢視訓練策略

links.title: Autonomous Mathematical Discovery in an Open-World Multi-Agent Environment

evidence: Section 3.1: 'all instances contain six research agents, two each powered by GPT-5.5, Claude Opus 4.8, and Gemini 3.1 Pro' and 'Most instances run for approximately 1,000-2,000 ticks, corresponding to roughly one to two weeks of continuous wall-clock operation.'

Section 2: 'The complete source code is openly available at https://github.com/dualverse-ai/station'; Section 3.2: 'All supporting proofs, verification artifacts, and raw agent dialogue are available at https://github.com/dualverse-ai/station_data_v2.'

Abstract/Section 3.2: five of 12 AlphaEvolve problems produced results novel relative to prior literature, including a new infinite family of finite-field Kakeya sets and 604-point kissing configurations in dimension 11 (Section 4.3).
Section 4.11: 'The Station reached only C6.2 <= 1.504473, worse than both AlphaEvolve and the current frontier' - honest reporting of underperformance versus baseline.

Section 5.5: three independent Station instances on the d=11 kissing-number problem all reached N=604, 'indicating that the improved lower bound is reproducible', with substantial path variance noted.
Section 4.13 (Discussion): first two Book Ramsey infinite families were autonomous discoveries, but the Yamada-Pott family 'required human expert involvement' since 'the agents did not connect them'.
Section 6: acknowledged limitations include 'Lack of expert intuition', 'Limited in-context learning', and 'Attractor traps'.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core contribution is an open-world multi-agent LLM environment (GPT-5.5, Claude Opus 4.8, Gemini 3.1 Pro researchers with coding assistants, archive papers, Question Room, holidays, multistart) applied to autonomous mathematical discovery, strongly matching the high-weight Agents & Tool Use, LLMs, and Reasoning preferences. Methodology novelty is moderate: the Station builds on the authors' prior v1 system (cited as [16]), with incremental mechanism additions, though the decentralized knowledge-accumulating design is distinctive versus pipeline agents. Rigor is high: careful comparisons against AlphaEvolve, HorizonMath, and a reconstructed pre-AlphaEvolve baseline (Appendix B), per-problem limitations, honest negative results (Sections 4.11-4.12 where the Station underperforms), and a reproducibility study (Section 5.5). Evidence strength benefits from released verification code and hedged novelty claims, though much self-verification remains. Generalizability is limited by the need for automated scorable evaluators; generality beyond math is asserted, not demonstrated here. Reproducibility is aided by open source and full dialogue release but depends on proprietary frontier models and 1-2 week runs with high variance.

primary_link.title: Autonomous Mathematical Discovery in an Open-World Multi-Agent Environment

Agents choose their own research directions, conduct experiments, collaborate, and build a shared scientific literature. Across 12 construction problems from the AlphaEvolve catalogue and two additional case studies, the Station obtained results novel relative to the prio
papers.summary_zh: 本文在「Station」開放世界多代理環境中研究 AI 的自主數學研究能力。該環境不設中央協調者，來自 GPT、Claude、Gemini 等模型家族的代理自行選擇研究方向、執行實驗、互通訊息並發表論文，累積為共享科學文獻。針對 AlphaEvolve 目錄的 12 個問題及兩個案例研究，Station 在五個問題上取得超越既有文獻的新結果：為 p≡3 (mod 4) 的質數證明新的有限體 Kakeya 集無窮族並改進 𝔽₃⁵ 的 53 點紀錄、建構三個精確的 11 維 604 點親吻組態、改進離散化 Kakeya 針與符號不確定性問題的上界，並將 Erdős 最小重疊問題的下界由 0.37912 提升至 0.380552。代理亦發現 Book Ramsey 數的新無窮族，並在一天內以純二元任務獨立重建雅可比猜想的七次反例。中繼分析顯示逾半數發現涉及跨模型家族協作，Claude 代理貢獻最多主要發現，假日與論文檔案機制最為關鍵。限制包括缺乏專家直覺、研究品味多樣性不足與吸引子陷阱。整體展示了開放自主環境可產出可解釋、可驗證且可累積的數學成果，為 AI 驅動的科學研究提供透明紀錄。
